review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–747). It has no definitions, structures, abbreviations or `@[simp]` lemmas, and it adds no simp-set entries. Every declaration is an existential analytic estimate: `exists_eLpNorm_rpow_le_mul_eLpNorm_rpow`, `exists_eLpNorm_le_ofReal_rpow_mul_eLpNorm`, the private `..._of_ball_subset` step, `exists_eLpNorm_le_mul_rpow_mul_eLpNorm`, and the averaged theorem with its private `_of_pos` helper. Each has the form `∃ C, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ ...`. None is a rewrite identity that simp could use as a rule. Its proofs call `simp only [...]` with explicit lemma lists (for example `simp only [I, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, Real.rpow_two, ...]`) and `simp [rk, pk]`, and I saw no sign these depend on a missing or badly oriented simp lemma. The empty-ball case is written out twice. That duplication is a proof-reuse matter, not a simp-interface defect. Adding simp attributes to these existential theorems would not be appropriate. The rubric therefore has no suitable target here. I did not check how other files use these theorems, because nothing in this file gives a simp interface to review.
